title: Fence Painting & Staining in Dunnellon, FL
description: Fence painting and staining in Dunnellon, FL: picket fences on historic lots, wood privacy fences, and faded vinyl, cleaned, repaired, and coated to last.
h1: Fence Painting and Staining in Dunnellon, FL
heroIntro: A white picket fence in front of a historic home and a cedar privacy fence around a backyard need completely different treatment. We handle both, along with vinyl that has faded or chalked.

questions: How do you repaint a picket fence without it peeling again?
Should a privacy fence be stained or painted?

sections.h2: Three fence types we see in Dunnellon
body: Fence painting in Dunnellon, FL usually falls into one of three jobs, and each starts in a different place. All three are regular work for our team in Dunnellon.
bullets: Painted picket fences, common in front of the older homes in Historic Downtown
Wood privacy fences around backyards in Rainbow Lake Estates, Rolling Hills, and Rio Vista
Vinyl fences that have yellowed, chalked, or grown mildew

sections.h2: Painted pickets: fixing the peel cycle
body: Picket fences peel because every picket has two faces, two edges, and a top cut that drinks water. If only the street side was painted last time, moisture enters from the back and pushes the paint off. We scrape loose paint, sand edges smooth, prime bare wood including the tops and backs, and finish with a 100% acrylic that flexes with the wood. Rotted pickets and posts are replaced before painting, not after.
Picket fences often match the house trim, so they pair naturally with exterior painting on your Dunnellon home.

Large backyard fences are better served by a penetrating stain. It soaks into the wood, does not peel, and is far easier to maintain later. We clean off mildew and gray fibers, let the wood dry, repair loose or broken boards, and spray the stain before back-brushing it into the grain. Semi-transparent and solid opacities are both options; solid hides past repairs, while semi-transparent shows the grain.
Sun and moisture both take a toll on unprotected fences. Our article on how Florida weather affects exterior coatings explains why timing and product matter.

Vinyl does not rot, but it does fade and gather mildew. Often a thorough soft wash is all it needs. When the color is gone, vinyl can be painted with a product system designed for it, as long as the fence is cleaned well and the new color is not so dark that it absorbs excess heat.

sections.h2: Small habits that protect the new finish
body: Once the fence is done, a few habits keep it looking right longer. Turn sprinkler heads so they water the lawn, not the pickets. Keep vines and shrubs trimmed back so the boards can dry after rain. Rinse pollen and dirt off the lower boards when you hose down the driveway. Small spots of wear on a stained privacy fence can be refreshed without redoing the whole run, as long as they are caught early.

Fence work fits the October-to-May window best, with summer jobs started early. If the house is being painted too, we do the fence after, so drips land on unfinished boards. A pre-clean through our Dunnellon soft washing service is often the first step. More product detail is on our Florida deck and fence staining page.

faqs.q: Why does my picket fence keep peeling?
faqs.a: Usually because the backs, edges, or tops were never sealed, so water gets in from behind. A proper repaint primes and coats every face.

faqs.q: Can you paint a vinyl fence?
faqs.a: Yes, with a product system made for vinyl, after a thorough cleaning. Very dark colors are not recommended on vinyl.

faqs.q: Do you replace broken fence boards?
faqs.a: Yes. Loose boards are re-fastened and damaged pickets or boards are replaced during prep.
